what_happened: All three countermodel grades, both transfer theorems, and a language-generic CountermodelEntry type compile-verified in two probe files on the first/second attempt: the gate theorem repackaged on explicit branch data (no kernel tableau rebuild) gives a kernel-checked gated-tableau entry with axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

The plan's Lean Challenge Statements block cross-validated against the Goals identifier set and COMPILED against the project's own toolchain on the first attempt (lean-challenge-snapshot.sh 973 . --dry-run --compile, exit 0), confirming every pinned signature's namespaces resolve (PointTruth, GenericValidIn, Branch, TimeOrdering, ofFormula) before any implementation dispatch runs. Compile-checking the Challenge block at plan time is cheap and catches the namespace errors the research report itself hit twice.

All 8 non-final phases' first-draft Tier Justification lines claimed the no-suite sentinel, which validate-artifact.sh rejected as a false claim. Root cause measured: plan-file-scope-harvest.sh auto-appends typst/generated/status.typ to EVERY phase carrying a .lean edit (this repo declares it a coupled generated surface), and that path maps to two real suites (test-plan-file-scope-harvest.sh, test-validate-artifact.sh). So a Lean-repo phase's selector output is always MIXED even when every named path maps to nothing. Corrected all 8 to name the two real suites; plan now validates with 0 warnings.

Backtick-delimited identifier lists written as annotation prose inside a Files to modify entry (e.g. 'new: `A`, `B`, `C`') are read by validate-artifact.sh as a comma-joined second path and warned on in 3 phases. Fix: annotation prose in Files to modify blocks carries no backticks at all. Worth knowing for any plan whose deliverables are named declarations.

Pre-task baseline of scripts/check-module-invariants.sh exits 1 on a C16 roots-baseline FAIL: 5 entries above the pinned ceiling in scripts/c16-roots-baseline.txt, all pre-existing and all out of this task's scope (BimodalLibTest.DiagnosticsTest docBlame x1; BimodalTools.CanonicalWire.Json defsWithUnderscore x3; BimodalTools.ForwardProofGenerator defsWithUnderscore x1; BimodalTools.JsonParse docBlame x8; BimodalTools.TableauBridge docBlame x4). Captured at commit a76a46f6e before any edit, so Phase 9's delta reading has a real baseline. Consequence for this task: BimodalLibTest IS a counted root, so every declaration in the Phase 8 test modules must carry a docstring or the ceiling grows.

All seven research probe files (P1-P7) survived in the session scratchpad at probe/, so Phases 1, 2, 5 and 6 start from compile-verified source rather than re-derivation. Phase 1's module built green with --wfail on first attempt.

lakefile.toml line 34 declares defaultTargets = ["FormalSystem"] only; BimodalLib, BimodalLibTest and BimodalTools are deliberately absent (header comment at lines 6-19). Measured: a bare guarded 'lake build --wfail' ran 3018 jobs and did NOT elaborate BimodalLib.Countermodel, while 'lake build BimodalLib --wfail' ran 3046 and did. Consequence: in THIS repository a bare full 'lake build' is a strictly WEAKER phase-end gate than the plan's scoped invocation, not a stronger one. The phase-end full-build gate is therefore discharged here as 'lake build BimodalLib BimodalLibTest --wfail', which transitively builds FormalSystem and every downstream dependent of the modules this task adds.

Phase 2 axiom measurement came in STRICTLY SMALLER than the plan's predicted [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]: not_genericConsequenceIn_of_le -> [propext]; not_genericConsequenceIn_ofFormula -> [propext, Quot.sound]; genericConsequenceIn_nil -> [propext, Quot.sound]; inferenceProfile_map_ofFormula -> [propext]. No Classical.choice anywhere, because both transfer theorems are explicit terms rather than classical tactic proofs.

Phase 2's first build failed: 'simpa [inferenceProfile] using profileP_ofFormula' left the goal as HasProfile.profile (ofFormula phi) = HasProfile.profile phi, which profileP_ofFormula does not match syntactically because the class projection does not unfold under simp. Fixed forward with two named rfl lemmas (hasProfile_eq_profileF / hasProfile_eq_profileP) added to the simp set, rather than with an inline 'show' -- 'show' is linted in this package and CI builds with --wfail. The two lemmas are deliberately NOT marked @[simp], to keep the class projection opaque elsewhere.

Phase 3's Scope Hypothesis predicted ~21 registrable hand-built refutations (16 class-tag plus 5 PlusValid). Measured by exact-name sweep: 20 declarations in the three sharpness modules match a class-tag non-validity shape, but 6 of those are schematic *_minFrameClass_sharp statements over a quantified fc with an fc < C hypothesis, which cannot be filed at a fixed frameClass; and the remaining 14 concrete declarations collapse to 6 entries once the plan's own MAXIMAL-class-only filing rule is applied (ZTime {density, dense_indicator}, Dense {prior_U_gap, sep}, RTime {prior_UZ, z1}). With the 5 PlusValid rows the landed total is 11, not 21. The hypothesis double-counted exactly what the maximal-class rule exists to collapse: Base/Dense/RTime duplicates of the same inference.

The research report recorded refute_determined's bounded object as 'the paper's Determined schema -- not formalized', implying a bare note with no nearMiss. Reading PlusNonValidities.lean's own docstring found that the POSITIVE half IS a theorem: FormalSystem.PlusLanguage.determined_of_deterministic (PlusDeterminism.lean:180) validates the schema on every Deterministic frame. That declaration is exactly what dropping the side condition refutes, so the row names a real declaration and 4 of the 5 stability refutations carry a resolvable nearMiss instead of 3.

Phase 4's third task instructed: 'Record in the entry's note that this entry's premises list is non-empty, and that it is the only landed entry for which that is true.' Measured FALSE: botUntlFamily is declared 'WitnessFamily ([] : Context) [botUntl]' at FormalSystem/Metalogic/Decidability/PlusSlicedCertificate/EmbedComplete.lean:813, so the entry's premises is []. Compiled probe confirms cmBotUntl.premises.length = 0. The research report had said only that this is 'the one entry whose refutation reaches the shape through a predicate that takes a premise list natively' -- a claim about not_consequence_ztime's SIGNATURE, which the plan over-read into a claim about this entry's own Gamma. Executed by writing the TRUE fact into the note and annotating the plan checklist item as 'deviation: altered'. Consequence: NO landed entry in this task has a non-empty premise list, and the Gamma slot of GenericConsequenceIn is exercised only by the transfer theorems and the lookup, not by any registered row.

A docstring placed BEFORE an 'open X in' prefix fails with "unexpected token 'open'; expected 'lemma'": the 'open ... in' prefix must precede the docstring, because the docstring is part of the declaration syntax the prefix wraps. Correct order is 'open X in / open Y in / /-- doc -/ / def f ...'. Also measured: a Python triple-quoted replacement string silently eats a Lean string-literal line continuation ('\\' at end of line becomes a Python line join), collapsing a wrapped note field into one 367-character line and tripping the 100-character limit. Edit-tool replacement avoids both.

Phase 5's Scope Hypothesis predicted the gate discharge would need 'set_option maxRecDepth 10000' and about 11 seconds of whole-file elaboration. Measured against a warm build: 'decide' closes gates_ok at the DEFAULT maxRecDepth of 512 -- probes at 512, 1000 and 2000 all compiled, and the module builds with no set_option at all -- and the module elaborates in 1.0-2.8 seconds. The unnecessary bump was removed rather than carried over from the research probe, because an unneeded recursion ceiling hides a later regression in exactly the quantity it was raised to protect. Branch measured at 14 signed formulas over 4 distinct times [3,2,1,0] and 1 world, with a 3-constraint ordering -- matching the research measurement exactly. Files are 123 and 99 lines, so the 1500-line longFile baseline task was not triggered.

BimodalLib/Countermodel/Lookup.lean failed to synthesize PointTruth Formula and PointTruth PlusFormula. Cause: BimodalLib/Countermodel.lean imports FormalSystem.Semantics.ValidityLayer, which declares the CLASS but not the instances -- those live at FormalSystem/Semantics/Validity.lean:211 and FormalSystem/PlusLanguage/PlusValidity.lean:71. The entry modules of Phases 3-5 never hit this because each imports an Independence or PlusLanguage module that pulls the instances in transitively; Lookup.lean is the first module to name a concrete CountermodelEntry type without such an import. Fixed by importing both instance-bearing modules directly. Also: BimodalLib/Subsumption.lean needed 'open FormalSystem.PlusLanguage (PlusFormula)' -- a single-name open rather than the whole namespace, since the extended language's defined operators share spellings with the base language's and would shadow them in that file.

A multi-line structure instance written as 'return { a := x, b := y,' with continuation lines indented 4 spaces fails with 'unexpected identifier; expected }': the opening brace puts the first field at column 12, so continuation lines at column 5 are LESS indented and terminate the instance. The error column points at the end of the accepted line, not at the offending token, which sends you looking for a reserved-token clash instead. Fix: put the brace alone at the end of its line and indent all fields uniformly, as BimodalLib/Index.lean's existing indexRow already does. Also measured: a Name set with the double-backtick form reads back as an Expr headed by the CONSTRUCTOR Name.str, not by Name.mkStr, so Registry.lean's nameOfExpr? returns none on it; a companion reader handling Name.anonymous/Name.str/Name.num was needed.

Rendering a countermodel row's inference with 'reduce' expanded every defined tense operator into its Until/Since/negation primitives, producing single table cells over 1000 characters (cmSep's ran to roughly 1100). Switching to 'whnf' unfolds only the head def, so the statement prints as '(schemaVar 0).allFuture.imp (schemaVar 0)' instead -- and that also matches what the theorem half's statementString already does, since it pretty-prints the declaration's type without reducing. The INDEX.md Countermodels section is 80 lines.

Measured, and recorded in the test: gates_ok -- the decide discharge of the eight branch gates -- depends on [propext] ALONE, not on the [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] triple every entry carries. So the gated-tableau grade's CHECKING step is classical-choice-free; the triple enters only through the bridge theorem not_valid_of_hasOpen_int that consumes it. The plan predicted the triple for the entry (correct) and the test now pins both figures separately, so a regression in either is visible.

Measured on this package: linter.style.longLine applies to CODE lines in Tests/ but NOT to docstring lines. A #guard_msgs expected-output docstring of 135 characters drew no warning, while two 107/111-character code lines in GateAgreementTest.lean each drew 'This line exceeds the 100 character limit' -- which --wfail turns into a build failure. Existing precedent confirms both halves: Tests/BimodalLibTest/DiagnosticsTest.lean carries a 429-character docstring line and builds clean, while Tests/BimodalTest/Metalogic/KTypeSummaryAxiomTest.lean uses 'set_option linter.style.longLine false in' for a 104-character #print axioms CODE line. Fixed by a two-name scoped open rather than a set_option, so no linter exemption was added.

Adding BimodalLib/Countermodel/Transfer.lean collided by BASENAME with FormalSystem/Metalogic/WeakCanonical/Transfer.lean and silently broke C20 for three citations in two UNRELATED FormalSystem files (ChronicleMonadicBridge.lean:572,576 and TruthTransfer.lean:119 each cited a bare 'Transfer.lean:NNN' that flipped from resolvable to ambiguous), pushing two (path, category) pairs past their pinned ceilings in scripts/c20-residual-baseline.txt. A concurrent writer fixed it forward in commit 0579cf458 and recorded it as the THIRD occurrence of the same mechanism (the earlier two were BimodalLib/Conservativity/Table.lean and the four BimodalLib/Theorems/*/Base.lean files). Checked the rest of this task's new basenames against FormalSystem: Countermodel.lean, Gates.lean, Lookup.lean, GatedTableau.lean, CountermodelTest.lean, GateAgreementTest.lean and UnresolvedNearMiss.lean are each unique; Complete.lean was already 3-way ambiguous before this task made it 4-way, so it introduced no new ambiguity class. Nothing warns at the point a new BimodalLib module is added -- a basename-collision pre-check on new module paths would catch this class before CI does.

A concurrent writer was editing scripts/module-invariants-allowlist.txt at the same time as this dispatch, for the same C5 failure. Both of us appended FormalSystem.PlusLanguage.PlusAxiom and FormalSystem.Metalogic.Decidability.WitnessFamily.Refutes; my append created exact duplicates, caught by 'grep -v ^# | sort | uniq -d' before committing. Kept their better-documented entries and removed mine. They had also allowlisted BimodalLib.Grade for a records/theorem-library.md citation, so the dotted form was kept there rather than rewritten to a bare name, which would have left their exemption dead in a file whose header says it is not a debt ledger. Separately, I allowlisted BimodalLib.CountermodelEntry for five BimodalLib/Countermodels/**/README.md files the same writer added, then C5's own 'allowlist entries no longer occur; prune them' INFO showed they had already switched those READMEs to the bare name, so that entry was pruned again. Net allowlist change from this dispatch: zero lines.

verify-touched.sh derives its touched-path set from the whole working tree, so with a sibling dispatch active it selected 87 agent-system shell suites over that sibling's untracked .githooks/* files rather than over this task's Lean and docs changes. The battery ran 8+ minutes with no log growth (its two serialized load-sensitive suites, test-gate-lock.sh and test-run-all-parallel.sh, were in flight) and was torn down before reporting, per dispatch-report-not-termination. Two run-all.sh children survived the parent kill and needed killing by PID; both carried this dispatch's own --timings path, so neither was the sibling's. The scoped discharge of record is therefore verify-deploy.sh --only-gate 4 --skip-unchanged (PASS, 0 failures) plus every repository-specific check Phase 9 names by name.
